findings.quote: **Combustion** is burning: a fast reaction with oxygen that gives off energy.
findings.problem: This definition makes oxygen necessary for combustion. Other oxidizers can support combustion. Hydrogen burns in fluorine without oxygen, so the definition would cause students to reject a valid combustion reaction.
findings.source: [NASA, Rocket Laboratory: Laying the Hydrogen Foundation](https://www.nasa.gov/rocket-laboratory-laying-the-hydrogen-foundation/), describes hydrogen engines tested with both oxygen and fluorine.

findings.quote: The hydrogen of the fuel still forms water.
findings.problem: This is not a general rule for incomplete combustion. With limited oxygen, methane can produce hydrogen gas and carbon monoxide: CH4 + 1/2 O2 → CO + 2H2. The statement incorrectly requires the fuel's hydrogen to become water in every oxygen-limited reaction.
findings.source: [U.S. Department of Energy, Hydrogen Production: Natural Gas Reforming](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/fuels/hydrogen-production-natural-gas-reforming), section Partial Oxidation.
